reason: The cited evidence discusses general wear protection by oxide layers in CCAs and other alloys, but none specifically demonstrates Si-induced amorphous SiO₂ film formation, its self-healing nature, or the claimed quantitative friction/wear reductions in CoCrFeMnNi. The premises rely on mechanisms and outcomes not directly supported by the provided passages.
premises: Si addition to CoCrFeMnNi will oxidize during heat treatment to form a continuous amorphous SiO₂ film
The SiO₂ film will be nano-scale, self-healing, and located on grain boundaries and worn surfaces
The SiO₂ film will reduce friction by ~40% and wear by ~50% from RT to ~700°C
The film will remain stable and continuous up to ~700°C
The oxidation treatment (850°C/1h) will produce this film without degrading mechanical integrity
